text: Osimertinib is a third-generation, irreversible, ATP-competitive tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that selectively targets the EGFR T790M resistance mutation in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mechanistically, it forms a covalent bond with the Cys797 residue in the ATP-binding pocket of the EGFR kinase domain, effectively locking the receptor in an inactive conformation and abolishing downstream oncogenic signaling (RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK and PI3K-AKT pathways). Unlike first- and second-generation TKIs, Osimertinib exhibits a high binding affinity and potency for both sensitizing EGFR mutations (ex19del, L858R) and the T790M resistance gatekeeper mutation, while displaying low affinity for wild-type EGFR. Clinically, this high mutant selectivity provides a robust therapeutic window, markedly suppressing tumor growth in T790M-driven NSCLC while minimizing dose-limiting off-target toxicities (e.g., severe rash and diarrhea) associated with wild-type EGFR inhibition.
